content.comment_body: Hello, After a power outage, the value of the UP/Down Counter gets lost. I tried using Node-RED, detecting when the [product_name] restarts, then injecting a numerical value into the initial parameter, but it didn't work. Is there a way to keep the counter value after a power cut? I have included both the Node-RED code and the [product_name] program with an unsuccessful attempt to rewrite the counter value in db1.dw16, which stores the initial value. Thank you for your assistance.
In the block properties of the counter, you need to enable retentivity to preserve its value.

analysis.insight_summary: The user mentioned that the UP/Down Counter in their [product_name] setup loses its state after a power failure. They tried but failed to restore the value with Node-RED. Another participant suggested setting retentivity for the counter block properties as the correct solution, indicating that this important feature was initially missed. The conversation spotlights a gap in user awareness regarding how to safely retain counter values after power loss.
analysis.user_expectations: User expects the [product_name] counter to sustain its value following power outages and to have a method for automatic restoration or retention of the most recent counter state.
